sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: Shift from 'Policing' to 'Partnership' model, initiated formally by the **1988 National Forest Policy**.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: **Usufruct Rights**—communities receive non-timber forest produce (NTFP) and a share of timber revenue in exchange for protection.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: **Institutional Framework**—involves the formation of Forest Protection Committees (FPCs) or Village Forest Committees (VFCs) at the grassroots level.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: **Benefit Sharing Mechanism**—the ratio of revenue sharing between the state and the community is determined by individual state-level JFM resolutions.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Key Application 1**: **Regeneration of Degraded Forests**—JFM is specifically targeted at degraded forest lands rather than pristine protected areas.
• **Key Application 2**: **NTFP Integration**—Linking forest protection with local livelihoods through the collection of honey, tendu leaves, and medicinal plants.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Elite capture of committees, lack of legal status for FPCs, and conflict with the Forest Rights Act (FRA) 2006.
• **Solutions**: Institutionalizing FPCs under the Gram Sabha and ensuring convergence with MGNREGA for forest-based employment.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'J-P-R' (Joint-Participatory-Regeneration).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Joint (Partnership), Participatory (Community-led), Regeneration (Focus on degraded lands).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: JFM is NOT a statutory act passed by Parliament; it is a policy framework initiated by the 1988 National Forest Policy and implemented via state-level resolutions.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Community-Based Natural Resource Management (CBNRM)' to elevate your answer quality.

keyTakeaways: JFM is a policy-driven, not act-driven, framework.
It focuses on degraded forests and benefit-sharing.
It represents a paradigm shift from 'State-controlled' to 'Community-participatory' forestry.
